boundary: Dated editorial follow-through using the exact September 22 source checks retained with the annual case. This is not a new source retrieval, an appellate merits review, independent article acceptance, or proof of construction, energization or customer service. The original publication and capture dates, record status, source profiles and October 1 Loudoun standards appointment are unchanged.

prior.title: Golden-Mars transmission approval still carries a local route condition
prior.summary: The Virginia State Corporation Commission approved the Golden-Mars transmission project in April 2026, while the preferred route remains subject to a Loudoun County School Board land decision and an alternate route remains available.
dependencies: school-board land decision or alternate route
final engineering and rights of way
local_implications: A state approval advances the project but does not establish a final built route or delivered customer capacity.

current.title: Golden-Mars Route 3A order is located; appeal and delivery remain separate
current.summary: The June 29, 2026 SCC order approves Route 3A. The July 20 order declines suspension, and the official docket checked September 22 lists Under Appeal. These records do not establish completed land arrangements, construction, energization or customer service.
dependencies: incorporated April conditions and map/CPCN compliance
land rights and later court or appellate orders
local_implications: The located route order resolves the earlier request to find a route decision, not the separate evidence gaps for compliance, land rights, physical completion or delivered customer capacity.

sections.heading: Evidence Stage
paragraphs: The SCC's June 29, 2026 Final Order in PUR-2025-00056 approves Route 3A, incorporates its April 9 order and specifies a subsequent map/CPCN process. The July 20 order declines suspension; it does not cancel the transmission approval.

The official docket checked September 22 lists Under Appeal. This is a dated case-status field, not an appellate merits ruling, evidence that no stay exists, or confirmation of unrestricted construction authority. The incorporated April conditions, later compliance, Supreme Court docket and appeal merits were not fully inspected. Construction, energization and customer service remain unproved by these records.

sections.heading: What To Watch Next
paragraphs: Follow map/CPCN compliance, the incorporated April conditions, land rights and subsequent court or appellate orders. Seek separate construction, inspection, energization and customer-service records before advancing a physical or service claim. The separate October 1 Loudoun standards appointment is unchanged.
